items.name: Espacio Gropius
items.summary: A coworking space in Mendoza. The site is built around one action: booking a room. Every section routes there instead of describing the place and stopping.

items.name: Matix Digital
items.summary: The agency I founded in 2025. Around 10 clients since then. I find them, scope the work, build the site and deliver it.

items.name: d2 Attention Test Calculator
items.summary: Scores the d2 attention test against age-banded reference values. Built for a psychology thesis where the correction was still done by hand. I found and fixed two calculation bugs in it: arguments passed in the wrong order, and numbers compared as strings.

items.name: Sales Management System
items.summary: Desktop sales system in Java over MySQL. I rewrote the write path to use PreparedStatement, which closed an SQL injection hole, and moved the database credentials out of the source code.

story.heading: The site got faster, then it started failing
body: A client site came to me for a performance pass at Spika Solutions. I optimized it and it did get faster. Then buffer errors started showing up that had not been there before.
I traced them to the WordPress configuration and fixed them there. The client kept the speed and lost the errors.
story.note: Most web work is not a blank page. It is taking over something that already exists and finding what is actually wrong with it.

steps.title: Start from the action
steps.body: What has to happen on this site: a booking, a call, a filled form. The layout follows that, not the other way around.

steps.title: Build it to be edited
steps.body: WordPress when the client needs to change things themselves. Hand-written HTML and CSS when speed is the point.

steps.title: Check it on a real phone
steps.body: Most visitors arrive on mobile. A site that only works on a laptop is not finished.

steps.title: Hand over the keys
steps.body: Domain, hosting and admin access go in the client's name. Nothing is held hostage.

about.heading: About
body: I started in technical support and sales, moved into web development at Spika Solutions in 2023, and in 2025 started my own agency.
Running it taught me the part most developers never touch: finding the client, agreeing on the scope, putting a price on it and being the one who answers when something breaks at 8pm.
I am looking for a stable role on a team, remote, working on one product instead of ten clients. My English is C1, certified, and I take client calls without an interpreter.
